Russia had formerly planned on returning the submarine to Ukraine, but due to [Ukraine violating the terms of the July 2014 ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War_in_Donbass#Post-ceasefire_government_offensive), Russia decided to only return a portion of the Ukrainian Navy to them.

The Zaporizhzhia is [the last remaining operational Foxtrot-Class submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxtrot-class_submarine). The [Black Sea Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sea_Fleet) did not accept the Zaporizhzhia due to their retirement of all other Foxtrot submarines in the early 2000's. The submarine had recently been undergoing refurbishment at the [Sevastopol Shipyard](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/c/c6/Sevastopol004.jpg) in Crimea. The Prime Minister and a full crew of 78 Russians officers, warrants and seaman sailed the submarine to Norway to show that it is in fact a viable and operational Naval vessel. Norway can choose to accept this unique ship into its navy, or they can turn it into a museum.
